post.topic: Frontend state management choice in modern web and mobile apps
post.linkedin_text:
Is Redux still worth using in 2026?

For years, adding Redux was the default first step for any React project. Boilerplate piled up before the first feature even worked.

Today, tools like React Context, Zustand, and Flutter's Provider or Riverpod let us build apps much faster without the ceremony.

Yet some large codebases still swear by strict global stores.

→ Simple state needs simple tools.
→ Global stores are rarely needed early on.

What is your go-to state management tool for new projects right now?

slides.title: Stop overcomplicating *State Management*
slides.body: When to use simple tools vs heavy global stores.

slides.title: Start local first
slides.body: Keep state inside the component until multiple distant components actually need it. Avoid premature global architecture.

slides.title: Embrace lightweight libraries
slides.body: Tools like Zustand in React or Riverpod in Flutter remove boilerplate while keeping your code clean and scalable.

slides.title: The danger of Redux everywhere
slides.body: Using massive global state stores for simple UI toggles or form inputs wastes time and slows down feature delivery.
